visualizerParams.title: Code Refactor: Keep the state in one variable
visualizerParams.problemDescription: The script reads the state back from the attribute each time. Keep it in a boolean variable and write the attribute and text from it. The button must behave the same.
visualizerParams.initialCode:
<button id="f" aria-pressed="false">Follow</button>
<script>
  var f = document.getElementById('f');
  f.addEventListener('click', function () {
    if (f.getAttribute('aria-pressed') === 'true') {
      f.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'false');
      f.textContent = 'Follow';
    } else {
      f.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true');
      f.textContent = 'Following';
    }
  });
</script>

solution.code:
<button id="f" aria-pressed="false">Follow</button>
<script>
  var f = document.getElementById('f');
  var following = false;
  f.addEventListener('click', function () {
    following = !following;
    f.setAttribute('aria-pressed', following);
    f.textContent = following ? 'Following' : 'Follow';
  });
</script>
solution.explanation: A boolean variable is the single truth about the state, and the page is written from it. Flipping it with ! is one line, and the two branches that repeated the same work disappear.

checks.label: One click gives Following and pressed
